question: Imagine you are a public health official tasked with drafting a community advisory on hereditary ovarian cancer risk. Integrate guideline facts about risk factors, genetic testing, and prevention strategies into your message.

question: Imagine you are a hematology fellow asked to write a detailed diagnostic summary for a patient with suspected chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Your summary should integrate the required laboratory and imaging tests, key biomarkers, risk assessment, and steps to confirm the diagnosis, as per the clinical practice guideline.
context_text:
(F1) "Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is a type of blood cancer, considered a form of cancer." -> CANCER_FORM_MATCHES_CLL_DEFINITION -> (F2) "Put together, chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a condition in your lymphocytes that doesn't go away." -> CLL_DEFINITION_INCLUDES_LYMPHOCYTIC -> (F3) "Lymphocytic means the condition occurs in the lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell." -> LYMPHOCYTIC_INVOLVES_B_LYMPHOCYTES -> (F4) "B cells, also called B lymphocytes, are one type of white blood cell."
(F5) "A CLL diagnosis requires at least 5,000 or more of the same white blood cells called monoclonal B lymphocytes to be found per microliter in your blood." -> DIAGNOSIS_CRITERIA_FOR_BLOOD_TEST -> (F6) "Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is confirmed with a blood test." -> UNCLEAR_BLOOD_RESULTS_TRIGGER_BIOPSY -> (F7) "If the blood results aren't clear, you'll have a biopsy of your lymph nodes or bone marrow to confirm CLL." -> LYMPH_NODE_BIOPSY_CONFIRMS_SLL -> (F8) "Tests of lymph nodes will also confirm small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL)."
(F9) "Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) often has a common pattern of surface proteins on its cells." -> CANCER_TYPE_IDENTIFIED_BY_IMMUNOPHENOTYPE -> (F10) "The way the abnormal cells look can be a clue as to what type of cancer you have." -> CANCER_TYPE_HINT_FROM_MICROSCOPY -> (F11) "The hematopathologist and your oncologist will examine a drop of your blood using a microscope." -> HEMATOPATHOLOGIST_EXAMINES_BLOOD_SAMPLES -> (F12) "The hematopathologist looks at blood, bone marrow, and lymph node samples for signs of disease."
(F13) "Most cells have an identifiable pattern of proteins, like a silhouette or a shape, called the immunophenotype." -> IMMUNOPHENOTYPE_IS_SURFACE_PROTEIN_PATTERN -> (F9) -> CLL_PROTEIN_PATTERN_INCLUDES_CD200_LEF1 -> (F14) "CLL cells have proteins called CD200 and LEF1, but another type of lymphoma, called mantle cell lymphoma, does not have them." -> CD200_LEF1_MATCH_CD20_PROTEIN_TYPE -> (F15) "An example of these proteins is CD20."
(F16) "For possible tests and procedures, see Guide 1." -> GUIDE_LISTS_PETCT_FOR_EXTRAMEDULLARY -> (F17) "FDG-PET/CT is a possible test if leukemia outside the blood and bone marrow (extramedullary) is suspected." -> FDG_PET_CT_IS_IMAGING_FOR_EXTRAMEDULLARY_LEUKEMIA -> (F18) "Imaging tests take pictures of the inside of the body to look for sites with leukemia outside the bone marrow."
(F19) "Right now, only a few targeted treatments are available for very specific kinds of glioma." -> FEW_TREATMENTS_LIMIT_TARGETED_OPTIONS -> (F20) "If testing detects a certain mutation, you might be able to receive treatment that's targeted more precisely to your glioma." -> TARGETED_TREATMENT_ENABLED_BY_TESTING -> (F21) "Biomarker testing can improve the accuracy of your diagnosis as well as fine-tune your treatment options."

(F25) "Treatment for CLL may not be needed for years, and some patients may never need treatment." -> NO_TREATMENT_NEEDED_DUE_TO_SLOW_GROWTH -> (F26) "CLL grows slowly." -> SLOW_GROWTH_MAKES_CURE_UNNECESSARY_GOAL -> (F27) "While the goal of treatment is not to cure CLL, the goal is to prevent the disease from causing problems and from becoming life-threatening."

(F30) "CLL stands for Chronic, Lymphocytic, and Leukemia."
(F31) "Write down questions and take notes during appointments; don't hesitate to ask your care team questions." -> TAKING_NOTES_AIDS_UNDERSTANDING_RESULTS -> (F32) "It is important you understand what these tests mean." -> UNDERSTANDING_TESTS_MOTIVATES_COPY_REQUESTS -> (F33) "Ask questions and keep copies of your test results."

(F5) -> THRESHOLD_SEPARATES_CLL_FROM_SLL -> (F37) "If a person has fewer than 5,000 cancerous cells in their blood, it is considered SLL." -> CELL_COUNT_DEFINES_SLL_VERSUS_CLL -> (F38) "A person with 5,000 or more monoclonal B lymphocytes per microliter in their blood is considered to have CLL."

question: You are a primary care physician referring a patient with newly diagnosed small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) to hematology/oncology. Write a referral note summarizing the clinical findings, diagnostic workup, relevant biomarkers, and rationale for referral, using the recommended guideline framework.
context_text:
(F1) "Important tests for primary CNS lymphoma include a neurological exam, imaging (MRI or CT scan), and biopsies." -> TESTS_CONFIRM_DIAGNOSIS -> (F2) "You'll need several tests to confirm whether you have primary CNS lymphoma or a lymphoma that started in another part of your body, or a different disease with similar symptoms." -> TEST_RESULTS_TRIGGER_TREATMENT_DISCUSSION -> (F3) "If these tests show that you have primary CNS lymphoma, your care team should discuss your treatment options with you." -> DIAGNOSIS_PRECEDES_TREATMENT_SELECTION -> (F4) "The main treatments for primary CNS lymphoma include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, stem cell transplant, or a combination of these treatments."
(F5) "For this book, treat any recommendation for CLL as one for SLL." -> IDENTICAL_TREATMENT_JUSTIFIES_BOOK_RECOMMENDATION -> (F6) "Treatment of CLL and SLL is the same because the cancer cells are the same." -> SAME_CANCER_EXPLAINS_IDENTICAL_TREATMENT -> (F7) "Small lymphocytic lymphoma, or SLL, is the same cancer as CLL." -> SAME_CANCER_DIFFERS_BY_CELL_LOCATION -> (F8) "The only difference between CLL and SLL is where the abnormal cells are found."
(F9) "Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is confirmed with a blood test." -> UNCLEAR_BLOOD_RESULTS_TRIGGER_BIOPSY -> (F10) "If the blood results aren't clear, you'll have a biopsy of your lymph nodes or bone marrow to confirm CLL." -> LYMPH_NODE_BIOPSY_CONFIRMS_SLL -> (F11) "Tests of lymph nodes will also confirm small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL)." -> CLL_SLL_CONFIRMATION_INCLUDES_LYMPH_NODE_TESTS -> (F12) "Tests that are needed for planning include physical exam including lymph nodes, spleen, and liver."

(F17) "Key points: treatment should start soon after being diagnosed with primary CNS lymphoma." -> START_SOON_AFTER_DIAGNOSIS -> (F18) "This chapter explains the phases of treatment, the options for each phase, and what to expect from the treatment process." -> TREATMENT_PHASES_SUPPORTED_BY_TEAM_CARE -> (F19) "Multidisciplinary care means that doctors, specialists, and allied health providers are working and communicating as a team to help you."
(F20) "For this reason, the disease is often referred to as CLL/SLL." -> CLL_SLL_LABEL_DUE_TO_SAME_CANCER -> (F7) -> SAME_CANCER_FOUND_IN_BLOOD_MARROW -> (F21) "CLL is mostly found in the blood and bone marrow." -> CLL_BLOOD_MARROW_CONTRASTS_SLL_LYMPH_NODES -> (F22) "SLL is mostly found in lymph nodes and the spleen."
